newsitem.title: USA: MESA Inc, Parker & Parsley to merge.
newsitem.headline: MESA Inc, Parker & Parsley to merge.

text.p: MESA Inc and Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co said on Sunday they signed a definitive agreement to merge and create Pioneer Natural Resources Co, a U.S. independent oil and gas exploration and production company.

Under terms of the agreement, MESA common stockholders would receive one share of Pioneer stock for every seven shares of MESA they held, and Parker & Parsley shareholders would receive one Pioneer share for each Parker & Parsley share, the companies said.
Pioneer's enterprise value would be about $4.2 billion based on Friday's closing share prices and including $1.3 billion in combined net debt outstanding, the companies said.
MESA shares ended up 1/8 at 5-3/4 on Friday, while Parker & Parsley shares finished up 7/8 at 29-7/8.
The companies were not immediately available to provide the deal's total value or to comment on any potential charges.

After the merger, Pioneer would have over 3.7 trillion cubic feet of natural gas equivalent reserves, comprised of 1.9 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 293 million barrels of crude oil and liquids, they said.
Pioneer's current daily production would be over 64,000 barrels of crude oil and natural gas liquids and 459 million cubic feet of natural gas, the companies said.
Its holdings would include the Hugoton gas field in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle and Spraberry fields in West Texas, the companies said.
Its reserve base would be 52 percent natural gas and 48 percent crude oil and liquids, they said.
"Pioneer will be the only independent that owns both long lived gas and long lived oil reserves and will have an aggregate reserve life index in excess of 12 years," they said.
Excluding recent and pending acquisitions, Pioneer's 1997 capital spending budget would be $400 million, to be directed at increasing production and reserves, the companies said.
Of this, Pioneer intended to invest $300 million to further develop existing reserves, they said.
About 600 wells would be drilled, and Pioneer expected to invest around $100 million to explore for new reserves using three dimensional seismic evaluation technology, they said.
MESA chairman and chief executive Jon Brumley would become Pioneer's chairman, the companies said.
Parker & Parsley chairman Scott Sheffield would become Pioneer's president and chief executive officer, they said.
Pioneer's management, directors and affiliates would own about 17 percent of the company's common stock upon completion of the merger, they said.

"MESA is paying a premium for a premium opportunity -- to create a major new independent with the size, strength and management expertise necessary to capitalize on the tremendous potential of MESA's long-lived natural gas reserves and Parker & Parsley's long lived oil properties," Brumley said.

Pioneer would be headquartered in Irving, Texas and have about 1,000 employees, they said. Pioneer would keep Parker & Parsley's operations in Midland, Texas and employment there was expected to increase.
It would also have significant operations in Amarillo, Houston and Corpus Christi, Texas, as well as in Oklahoma City and Lafayette, Louisiana, they said.
Richard Rainwater, a MESA director, would be the new company's largest individual shareholder.

Under terms of the deal, holders of MESA series A and B eight percent cumulative convertible preferred stock will have the option to receive either 1.25 share of Pioneer common stock for every seven shares held or one share of Pioneer series A eight percent cumulative convertible preferred stock for every seven shares held, they said.
Rainwater and his affiliates owned all the outstanding MESA series B preferred stock, MESA said.
The merger was subject to certain conditions.

If during the 15 trading days ended five trading days before the shareholder votes, MESA's average closing common stock price was less than $5 per share, each party would have the option to terminate the merger, they said.
